description: Search the issues visible to this token, with a JQL query — the same JQL the Jira REST surface takes, read by the same parser. A query naming a field this tracker does not have is REFUSED and named, never run: it would match everything and read as an answer. Without `jql`, the shorthand arguments filter instead. Most recently created first unless the query says ORDER BY. Archived issues are left out unless the query names `archived`, and `archivedLeftOut` says how many matches that hid — an empty list with it is not "there are none".

jql.description: A JQL query, e.g. `assignee = currentUser() AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY updated DESC`. FIELDS: project, status, statuscategory, issuetype, type, priority, resolution, assignee, reporter, creator, key, issuekey, id, summary, description, sprint, parent, epic, labels, archived, agent, teamRole, text, created, updated, duedate. OPERATORS: = != ~ !~ > >= < <=, IN (...), NOT IN (...), IS EMPTY, IS NOT EMPTY, combined with AND / OR, with parentheses around a sub-expression — `project = PM AND (status = Blocked OR priority = Highest)` — plus an optional trailing ORDER BY <field> [DESC]. `~` means contains (substring) and is the one to use for free text — `text` searches summary, description and comments. `>` `>=` `<` `<=` are for created/updated/duedate only, with absolute YYYY-MM-DD values: there are NO relative-date functions, so compute the date yourself. The functions are currentUser(), for assignee/reporter/creator, and myTeamRoles(), for teamRole. `archived` is this tracker's own field: archived issues are left out unless the query mentions it. `epic` is this tracker's own too, and it is the wide one: `epic = PM-12` matches that epic AND the work under it — its children and their sub-tasks — which is how one asks for an epic's whole board in a single clause. `parent` is the narrow one: direct children only, and never the epic itself. `agent` is this tracker's own as well: `agent = product` is an issue an agent of that role has right now — working on it or waiting on its question — and `agent IS NOT EMPTY` is any agent; the assignee of such an issue is still the person it works for. `teamRole` is this tracker's own too: the project's team role an issue is for, by name — `teamRole = "Звуковик"` — and `teamRole in myTeamRoles()` is every issue for a role the caller holds, which with `assignee != currentUser()` is the work of their role that fell to somebody else. Quote values containing spaces. Seeded values — status: Backlog, "To Do", "In Progress", "In Review", Blocked, Done; statusCategory: "To Do", "In Progress", Done; priority: Highest, High, Medium, Low, Lowest; type: Epic, Story, Task, Bug, "Sub-task". A project's own columns (PM-170) can be searched too, by name — Segment = AI — or as customfield_20003 / cf[20003]; list_project_fields names them.

projectKey.description: Shorthand for `project = …` (must be visible to the token). Narrows the query further when `jql` is given too.

status.description: Shorthand for `status = …` (e.g. 'In Progress', 'Done'). Narrows the query further when `jql` is given too.

text.description: Shorthand for `key ~ … OR summary ~ …`. Narrows the query further when `jql` is given too.

name: search_issues
